sources.name: QuillBot Help: free vs Premium Paraphraser

caption:
QuillBot is built to reword text. Grammarly is built to fix and polish it.
Free QuillBot paraphrases 125 words at a time in 2 modes. Free Grammarly checks mistakes and gives 100 AI prompts a month.
The full comparison with plans and steps is on neurafeedai.com.

Which one do you keep open while you write?

site_article.seo_title: QuillBot vs Grammarly: which writing AI to use in 2026
site_article.seo_description: QuillBot vs Grammarly compared: free plan limits, Premium and Pro prices, paraphrase modes, AI prompts, where each works and which one to pick for what.
site_article.answer_summary: Pick QuillBot if you mostly need to reword, paraphrase or summarize text. Pick Grammarly if you mostly need correct grammar, tone and style across email, Docs and Word. Both have free plans, so test your own writing in each first.

paragraphs.text: QuillBot vs Grammarly is mostly a question of what you do with your text. QuillBot is built around its Paraphraser: you paste text and it rewrites it in a mode you choose. Grammarly is built around checking what you already wrote for mistakes and tone, with AI rewrites on top. Each now does a little of the other's job, so the free and paid limits decide most cases.
QuillBot vs Grammarly at a glance

QuillBot's free plan lets you paraphrase up to 125 words at a time in two modes, Standard and Fluency, fix basic grammar errors, humanize text in a Basic mode, make basic summaries and use a limited AI Detector. Premium removes the word limit and unlocks all 9 built in modes, plus custom modes, a side by side Compare Modes view and a history of up to 50 paraphrases a month.

Grammarly's free plan checks for mistakes, shows the tone of your writing and includes 100 AI prompts a month. Pro adds full sentence rewrites, tone adjustment, plagiarism and AI text detection, and 2,000 AI prompts a month. Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, and the old Premium plan has been replaced by Pro.
Prices and free limits

QuillBot lists Premium at $8.33 a month billed annually, with a 3 day money back guarantee, and a Team plan without a public price on that page. Premium can be used on up to 10 devices at a time. The eesel AI pricing review lists the monthly Premium price at $19.95, which the official page did not show when NeuraFeed checked on November 27, 2026.

QuillBot's comparison table also shows the Summarizer at 1,200 words on the free plan and 6,000 words on Premium, and puts translation, paraphrasing in 23 languages and a plagiarism check of 25,000 words a month on the Premium side.

Grammarly lists Pro at $12 per member a month billed annually, or $30 billed monthly. Pro covers teams of up to 149 people and adds a style guide, brand tones, snippets and analytics. Enterprise is sold through Superhuman Go with unlimited prompts. eesel AI's review matches those Pro prices.
Where each one works

QuillBot lists a Chrome extension, an Edge extension, a macOS app, a Word add-in, and Android and iOS keyboards and apps. Grammarly lists desktop apps for Windows and Mac, browser extensions for Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge, Microsoft Office, Google Docs, and mobile apps for iPhone, iPad and Android.
How to test both in ten minutes

paragraphs.title: 1. Pick one real paragraph
paragraphs.text: Use something you actually wrote this week, around 100 words, so it fits QuillBot's free 125 word limit. A paragraph with one clumsy sentence works best.

paragraphs.title: 2. Run it through QuillBot's Paraphraser
paragraphs.text: Paste it into QuillBot and try Standard mode, then Fluency mode. Those are the two modes the free plan includes. Check whether the meaning stayed the same, not just whether it sounds smoother.

paragraphs.title: 3. Paste the same paragraph into Grammarly
paragraphs.text: Open it in Grammarly in your browser or in Google Docs. Look at the mistakes it flags and the tone it detects. On the free plan you get corrections and tone, not full sentence rewrites.

paragraphs.title: 4. Try one AI prompt in Grammarly
paragraphs.text: Use one of your 100 free monthly prompts to ask for a rewrite, then compare it with QuillBot's version side by side.

paragraphs.title: Prompt: a tighter version of your paragraph
paragraphs.text:
Rewrite this paragraph so it is shorter and clearer. Keep every fact and name exactly the same, and do not add anything new:
[paste your paragraph]

paragraphs.title: 5. Decide by what you fixed most
paragraphs.text: If you mostly changed wording, QuillBot fits. If you mostly fixed errors and tone, Grammarly fits. If you did both, start with free plans of each before paying for one.
Which one to pick

Pick QuillBot if your work is restating: summarizing sources, rewording a draft that sounds stiff, or trying several versions of one sentence. It is cheaper on a yearly plan, but the free plan's 125 word cap gets in the way fast on longer text.

Pick Grammarly if your work is writing every day in email, Docs and Word and you want it checked where you type. The free plan is useful on its own for catching mistakes. Pay for Pro only if you need full sentence rewrites, tone changes or the larger prompt allowance.
Neither tool knows your facts. After any rewrite, read it once for meaning: a smoother sentence that says something different is worse than a clumsy one that is right.
If you write for school or work rules that limit AI use, check those rules before you paraphrase someone else's text. Both tools list AI detection features, which tells you others can check too.
